title: Seventy percent is not a promise
logline: A 70% forecast means 3 in 10 go the other way — judge forecasts by calibration, and plan for the thirty.
audience: Busy professionals who read forecasts (delivery dates, pipelines, risk) but never learned how to read a probability.

music.prompt: Minimal modern ambient, soft felt piano, warm analog pads, a very light pulse

arc.The forecast: Intro: a single felt-piano figure over a soft pad, very sparse.
arc.A hundred launches: A light pulse enters; steady and patient, leaves room for the voice.
arc.Calibration: Same groove, slightly brighter pad; no new melody.
arc.The better question: Thin out to the pad alone for a moment of focus.
arc.Recap: Resolve: the piano figure returns once and settles on a sustained chord.

beats.vo: Seventy percent. <short pause> It sounds like a sure thing.
beats.visual: A serif '70%' rises out of a mask as the word is spoken; the caption 'chance the launch ships on time' follows.

beats.vo: It isn't. It means three times in ten, it won't.
beats.visual: 70% glides up and shrinks. A row of ten tiles builds; the last three turn cobalt on 'three'. '3 in 10' labels them.

beats.vo: Picture a hundred launches with that same forecast.
beats.visual: A 10×10 grid of dots blooms from the centre. Kicker: 100 launches · same 70% forecast.
Seventy dots fill in ink, row by row. Counter: 70 · on time.

beats.vo: About thirty slip. <short pause> That's not the forecast failing. It's the forecast working.
beats.visual: The remaining thirty light up cobalt. Counter: 30 · slip. 'working' is underlined as it's spoken.
Axes draw: 'Forecast said' vs 'Actually happened'. A dashed diagonal draws: perfectly calibrated.

beats.vo: Of everything called seventy percent, about seventy percent happens.
beats.visual: Points pop along the diagonal; the 70% point is marked: said 70 → happened 70.

beats.vo: Overconfident forecasts sag below the line.
beats.visual: A second curve in rust draws below the diagonal, labelled overconfident.

beats.vo: So don't ask whether the forecast was right. Ask whether you planned for the thirty.
beats.visual: 'Was the forecast right?' is struck through. 'Did we plan for the 30?' rises beneath it; '30' is highlighted.

beats.vo: Seventy is likely, not certain. Check calibration. And plan for the thirty.
beats.visual: Three numbered takeaways, each landing on its spoken phrase.
Title card: 'Seventy percent is not a promise.' Footnote: hypothetical illustration.
